questions: How are META_LEDGER entry numbers and previous_hash allocated?
What does the chain validator actually detect for duplicate entry numbers / duplicate previous_hash?
How were prior occurrences (#447 reconciliation of #397/#401) resolved?
Does upstream qor-logic expose a reservation/renumber surface for consumers?
What is the minimal correct resolution for the live Entry #597 collision?

findings.summary: Allocation is max(N)+1 over the LOCAL ledger (ledger_fragment.py:95-104); no reservation, no lock, no cross-branch check. Both sessions computed 597 correctly.

verify_post_anchor() returns exit 0 'post-anchor clean' on the both-merged forked ledger; _sequence_breaks is disarmed because verify() passes the raw _duplicate_previous_hash_members set as tolerated (ledger_hash.py:543-545). Falsified: emptying the tolerated set produces BREAK Entry #597.
18 pre-existing genuine duplicate entry numbers (#113,#204x3,#205x3,#218,#222-236); confirmed not fence artifacts. ledger_hash.ENTRY_RE and ledger_fragment._ENTRY_NUM_RE use different fence dialects.
Entry #447 RECONCILIATION is only a partial precedent: RECONCILED_ENTRIES_RE is number-keyed, so it cannot disambiguate two entries both numbered #597. No post-merge in-chain remedy exists.

Upstream ships the fix (ledger_fragment Phase 56 fragments; entry_id Phase 76). FailSafe adopted neither: .qor/ledger absent; 0 of last 12 entries carry the Entry ID line qor-substantiate/SKILL.md:382 declares MUST. Entry #447 has one - a regression.

Resolution verified: plan-233 (ts 2026-08-22) keeps #597, plan-430 (ts 2026-08-23) rebases to #598 per ledger_fragment.py:76 (ts,uid) sort. content_hash is number-independent and reproduces; only previous_hash/chain_hash change. Remediated ledger re-validated clean at boundary #598.
PR #434 changes production Sentinel source with NO META_LEDGER GATE entry and creates a new nested governance root FailSafe/.failsafe/ (0 files on main, 15 plans at the canonical repo-root path).
Entry #594 routed plan-233 to /qor-remediate 'NOT to a fourth plan iteration'; PR #433 delivers exactly that. The process defect #594 named is the same defect found in ledger_hash.verify().
